en.question: Your team wants shared, version-controlled Claude Code settings for the project, while each developer keeps personal overrides that are never committed. Which arrangement is correct?

options.text: Commit both files and rely on developers not to edit the shared one.
options.note: Committing personal overrides produces constant spurious diffs and conflicts.

options.text: Keep all settings in the user-level home directory configuration only.
options.note: User-level settings are not shared, so the project gets no common baseline.

options.text: Commit one settings file and have each developer maintain a local branch.
options.note: Long-lived config branches are a merge burden and drift immediately.

en.explanation: That split is exactly what the two filenames are for: shared project settings are committed, and the .local variant holds personal overrides and stays untracked.
